memory_update.text: VECO should be tracked as the cleanest US-listed underfollowed equipment candidate for compound-semiconductor photonics tools; key later-layer checks are backlog, MOCVD order quality, AI/InP specificity, and lead-time evidence.
AXTI should be tracked as a direct InP/GaAs substrate candidate; later layers must separate AI/datacenter optical demand from legacy telecom and assess export-control and China manufacturing risk.

COHR's InP and AI-datacom capacity commentary can serve as a reference signal for whether substrate/tool constraints are tightening or easing across the upstream optical networking stack.

US-listed universe has limited pure-play exposure to plasma etch/deposition, wafer bonding, and optical test specifically for III-V/CPO; future passes should search MKSI, ONTO, CAMT, AEIS, TER, KEYS, and foreign-listed Aixtron/Oxford Instruments as comparables or secondary mappings.

node: Compound-semiconductor photonics tools, substrates, epitaxy, etch, bonding, and test
summary: Layer 1B expanded the US-listed universe for the upstream optical-AI networking node. The strongest underfollowed discovery candidates are not transceiver mega-cap anchors but companies tied to MOCVD/compound-semiconductor tools, InP/GaAs substrates, and scalable III-V-on-silicon photonics platforms. COHR is included as a high-attention reference anchor because its public InP capacity commentary helps validate the bottleneck. VECO, AXTI, and ALMU are the discovery lane candidates to verify in later layers through backlog, order, customer, qualification, and revenue-conversion evidence.
